items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: when I studied at Berklee with Joe Viola, he stressed classical etudes

ctx.x: I’m trying to form a question here about what did you try to copy?

Oh boy, Trane, I mean the sound was one of the things that I’ve always been drawn to. His use of vibrato in the later period, you know where he was almost into a classical vibrato. You know when I studied at Berklee with Joe Viola, he stressed classical etudes

but not playing in that style. And so what I was always listening to the way Trane would use his vibrato, where he would play — usually a jaw vibrato but sometimes a jaw and a diaphragm combination vibrato. I heard Sonny Rollins doing the same thing where they combine the flute — ha-ha-ha-ha-ha — with the ya-ya-ya-ya jaw, so you get two things working at once. You get the depth of the stomach vibrato — ha-ha-ha-ha — that’s going here and there. It’s kind of tricky. I just picked it up. But I mean I just copied a…
